analyzed_vuln.description: `bitunshuffle()` calls the SIMD bitunshuffle backend with `size = blocksize / bytesoftype` (element count) for format_version==2, but for old-format bitshuffle data the backend expects a byte-multiple-of-8 style sizing convention. This mismatch lets crafted metadata drive the AVX2/SSE2 path (`bshuf_untrans_bit_elem_avx2` -> `bshuf_shuffle_bit_eightelem_sse2`) to compute output indices beyond the allocated temp/output buffer and perform out-of-bounds writes (crash at bitshuffle-sse2.c:445).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In `decompress_frame_fuzzer`, attacker-controlled frame/chunk header fields (typesize/blocksize/filter metadata/version path) reach `pipeline_d()` and then `bitunshuffle()`. With BITSHUFFLE enabled and format_version==2 on malformed legacy-style bitshuffle payload/size combinations, `bitunshuffle()` passes inconsistent size semantics to the backend, causing the SSE2 store loop to write past `out` (`out_ui16[ind/2]`). The PoV triggers this during `blosc2_getitem` while decoding a lazy chunk from the frame.
